name: Tunis
tagline: Mediterranean Charm, French-Arab Culture, and Incredible Value on the North African Coast
description: Tunis blends Mediterranean sophistication with North African warmth and affordability. The ancient medina is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the ruins of Carthage sit on the city's outskirts, and the beaches of La Marsa and Sidi Bou Said are among the most beautiful in the Mediterranean. French colonial architecture, excellent cuisine fusing Arab and French traditions, and a mild Mediterranean climate make Tunis a hidden gem for FIRE retirees. Costs are remarkably low, French is essential (English is limited), and the expat community is small but growing.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day visa-free stay for US citizens. Renewable residence permits available with proof of financial means. No dedicated retirement visa — residency through property purchase or proof of pension/passive income.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate to Good – generally safe in tourist and residential areas
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with hot dry summers and mild wet winters

housing.description: Modest 1BR in central Tunis or Le Bardo (non-coastal; rents a third of the coast)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking plus a few cheap local eats (couscous, brik, grilled fish)

healthcare.description: Basic local private cover, single adult 45–55

transportation.description: TGM light rail plus louage/taxi; no car

1M.lifestyle: A modest 1BR inland in central Tunis or Le Bardo, where rents run about a third of the coast. Most meals come from cheap, state-subsidized local staples cooked at home, with couscous, brik, and grilled-fish spots for the occasional meal out. Transport is the TGM light rail and shared louages or taxis — no car. Basic local private insurance covers Tunisian private clinics without long public-sector waits. Discretionary spending is thin, but the Mediterranean, the medinas, and café culture cost almost nothing, and French is essential.

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable furnished 1BR on the coast in La Marsa or Les Berges du Lac, walkable to cafés and the sea. Dining out several nights a week is easily affordable, and comprehensive local private insurance gives fast access to the best Tunisian private clinics. You skip car ownership but take taxis freely and rent a car for weekend trips to Sidi Bou Said or Cap Bon. Beach clubs, cinema, a gym, and an easy nightlife fill the weeks.

dining.description: Frequent quality dining at seafront restaurants, with wine

healthcare.description: Strong private plan approaching international cover

transportation.description: An owned car or unlimited taxis

entertainment.description: Clubs, events, plus amortized regional/European weekend travel

3M.lifestyle: A bright furnished 1BR or compact 2BR-for-one in a desirable coastal suburb — La Marsa, Gammarth, Sidi Bou Said, or Les Berges du Lac — with a car in the garage. You dine at the better seafront restaurants routinely, stock imported goods without thinking, and carry a strong private plan bordering on international cover. Periodic weekend hops to Europe are cheap and short (Rome, Paris, and Malta are quick flights), and clubs and events fill the rest. Costs remain a fraction of any European coastal equivalent.

5M.lifestyle: Upper-luxury for one — a high-end Gammarth apartment or a small seaside villa with a pool, kept by a near-full-time housekeeper who also cooks, with an occasional driver. Dining is near-daily at the best tables, and a top-tier private/international policy will medevac you to Europe if needed. A beach- or golf-club membership plus frequent short-haul European travel round out the lifestyle. Even here, Tunis delivers what would cost three or four times as much on the northern Mediterranean.

10M.lifestyle: The ceiling of what one person can plausibly consume in Tunis — a top-of-market luxury villa or apartment in Gammarth or Les Berges du Lac, scaled to a solo occupant rather than a family estate, with a full-time housekeeper, cook, and driver. Healthcare is an international concierge policy with medevac to Europe, and a premium car sits in the drive. The discretionary budget funds frequent European travel, events, VIP experiences, and fine wine and art. Tunisia's low wages and subsidized staples keep even this near $8.8k a month — and a solo person simply can't fill a household's bedrooms, meals, or estate staff.
